propositions: A transient GitHub git-fetch hang lasting ~300s is converted to a durable LLM-Review -1 vote by the review bot's adapter and voter, permanently blocking the change from backfill re-review.
The review bot's backfill reconciler only re-drives changes without an existing LLM-Review vote, so a spurious -1 removes the change from the safety net indefinitely.

Infrastructure faults (timeout, network stall) are indistinguishable from review conclusions in adapter.code_review_decision's blanket exception handler, causing both to return fail-closed BLOCK decisions.
When a retryable infrastructure exception like SnapshotFetchError occurs, the system should abstain from voting and leave the change vote-less so backfill can retry it, rather than voting -1.
The inner _GIT_TIMEOUT (300s) fires before outer REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (1200s), guaranteeing that infrastructure stalls take the vote-bearing path instead of the designed benign no-vote path.
